name: Carrot cake
origin: Grew from medieval European carrot puddings (sweetened with a genuinely scarce and precious sugar substitute) into a 20th-century oil-based spice cake; commonly finished with a cream-cheese frosting, itself popularised in the mid-20th-century United States.

ingredients.note: carrot cake is traditionally oil-based rather than butter-based, for a moist crumb that stays soft when chilled under cream-cheese frosting; see catalog.ts module notes

water fraction of grated carrot at 90% of flour mass, split by USDA raw-carrot composition (~88% water); real recipes vary widely in carrot quantity, 90% of flour mass is a representative middle figure
non-water fraction (fibre, sugars, colour) of the same grated carrot
chopped walnuts or pecans, a common but not universal addition; treated as flavour/bulk rather than split by composition since nuts contribute negligible free water

process.name: whisk oil, sugar and eggs
process.description: whisk oil, sugar and eggs to a smooth emulsion

process.name: fold in dry and carrot
process.description: fold in flour, leavening, salt and spice, then the grated carrot and nuts

process.name: bake
process.description: bake in round pans or a sheet tin

notes: Grated carrot's real water content (USDA FoodData Central, raw carrot: ~88 g water per 100 g) is split into its own liquid-role line so it is honestly credited toward the batter's hydration rather than treated as inert bulk, the same technique used for banana and pineapple elsewhere in this catalogue. Cream-cheese frosting is a separately-prepared component applied after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
